inline_comments.comment: `# creates: cu.png` is a leftover from ASE's old documentation build system, which parsed this directive to track generated output files. It has no special meaning in sphinx-gallery and will appear as a confusing no-op comment in the rendered page. The peer example `ptable.py` in the same gallery directory does not include such a comment. This line should be removed.

The single-letter variable `a` was copied from the old `doc/ase/dft/bs.py` but is a poor choice for a user-facing example. ASE convention uses `atoms` for `Atoms` objects — this is consistently applied in the peer example `ptable.py` (`atoms = ptable()`) and throughout ASE's own documentation. Renaming to `atoms` here also requires updating the subsequent three lines (`atoms.calc = ...`, `atoms.get_potential_energy()`, `bs = atoms.calc.band_structure()`).

The k-point path is specified via a plain dict (`kpts={'path': 'GXWLGK', 'npoints': 200}`), which is the older ASE API. The modern, more explicit form is `atoms.cell.bandpath('GXWLGK', npoints=200)`, which returns a typed `BandPath` object and makes the intent clearer to readers learning from this example. Using the modern API here also ensures the example stays current as the dict-based shorthand may be soft-deprecated.

general_comments.comment: The module docstring contains only the section title (`Band-structure`) with no descriptive text. While the peer example `ptable.py` follows the same minimal pattern, a gallery example is a primary learning resource. Adding even one or two sentences — e.g. explaining that this uses a free-electron model to compute and plot the band structure of FCC copper along a standard high-symmetry path — would meaningfully lower the barrier for newcomers and make the example self-contained.

No sphinx-gallery cross-reference label (e.g. `.. _galleryband:`) is present in the module docstring. Without it, other documentation pages cannot link directly to this example using the standard `:ref:` role. If any existing docs previously referenced the old `doc/ase/dft/bs.py` version of this script, those links will be silently broken unless a label is added here.
